## Loading packages

```{r}
# Set up renv for package management

}
```

## Data Loading and Handling

```{r}
# Define folder path and load raster files
folder_path_dev <- here("Data", "processed", "Worldpop_dev_indicators")
tif_files_dev <- list.files(folder_path_dev, pattern = "\\.tif$", full.names = TRUE)

# Load the mean raster files
raster_data_mean <- c(
  rast(tif_files_dev[grep("ANC_MEAN", tif_files_dev)]),
  rast(tif_files_dev[grep("INSURANCE_MEAN", tif_files_dev)]),
  rast(tif_files_dev[grep("MALNUTRITION_MEAN", tif_files_dev)]),
  rast(tif_files_dev[grep("PNC_MEAN", tif_files_dev)]),
  rast(tif_files_dev[grep("SBA_MEAN", tif_files_dev)]),
  rast(tif_files_dev[grep("TT_MEAN", tif_files_dev)]),
  rast(tif_files_dev[grep("DECISION_MEAN", tif_files_dev)]),
  rast(tif_files_dev[grep("HWEALTH_MEAN", tif_files_dev)]),
  rast(tif_files_dev[grep("MEDUCATION_MEAN", tif_files_dev)])
)

# Load all raster layers  using the rast function
raster_data_dev <- lapply(tif_files_dev, rast)
raster_data_dev1 <- lapply(tif_files_dev1, rast)
raster_data_pop <- lapply(tif_files_pop, rast)

# Load population raster file
KAMP_POPULATION_10m <- rast(here("Data", "processed", "Worldpop_density", "pop_total_10m.tif"))

# Normalize each layer individually
normalized_rasters <- lapply(1:nlyr(raster_data_mean), function(i) {
  layer <- raster_data_mean[[i]]  # Extract individual layer
  layer_min <- as.numeric(global(layer, fun = "min", na.rm = TRUE)[1])  # Layer-specific min
  layer_max <- as.numeric(global(layer, fun = "max", na.rm = TRUE)[1])  # Layer-specific max
  (layer - layer_min) / (layer_max - layer_min)  # Normalize
})

# Combine normalized layers back into a single SpatRaster
normalized_rasters_stack <- rast(normalized_rasters)

# Calculate the equal-weighted index (mean of all layers)
equal_index <- app(normalized_rasters_stack, fun = mean, na.rm = TRUE)

# Align all rasters to the population raster
# Align the normalized rasters to the population raster
aligned_rasters_normalized <- Spatial.align::align(
  normalized_rasters_stack, 
  KAMP_POPULATION_10m, 
  resample_method = "near"
)

# Align the mean raster to the population raster
aligned_rasters_mean <- Spatial.align::align(
  raster_data_mean, 
  KAMP_POPULATION_10m, 
  resample_method = "near"
)

# Align the index raster to the population raster
aligned_index <- Spatial.align::align(
  equal_index, 
  KAMP_POPULATION_10m, 
  resample_method = "near"
)


autoplot(aligned_rasters_normalized$UGA_HWEALTH_MEAN) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "magma", direction = -1) + # Using magma color scale with reversed direction
  labs(title = "Normalized Household Wealth Mean", fill = "Normalized Value") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "right", # Adjust legend position as needed
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5), # Center the title horizontally
    plot.margin = unit(c(1, 1, 1, 1), "lines"),
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white"), # Set plot background color to white
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white"), # Set panel background color to white
    panel.grid.major = element_blank(), # Remove major grid lines
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), # Remove minor grid lines
    axis.line = element_line(color = "black"), # Set axis line color to black
    axis.text = element_text(color = "black"), # Set axis text color to black
    axis.title = element_text(color = "black") # Set axis title color to black
  )

autoplot(aligned_index) +
    scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "magma", direction = -1) + # Using magma color scale with reversed direction
    labs(title = "Aligned Equal-Weighted Index", fill = "Normalized Value") +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      legend.position = "right", # Adjust legend position as needed
      plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5), # Center the title horizontally
      plot.margin = unit(c(1, 1, 1, 1), "lines"),
      plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white"), # Set plot background color to white
      panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white"), # Set panel background color to white
      panel.grid.major = element_blank(), # Remove major grid lines
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), # Remove minor grid lines
      axis.line = element_line(color = "black"), # Set axis line color to black
      axis.text = element_text(color = "black"), # Set axis text color to black
      axis.title = element_text(color = "black") # Set axis title color to black
    )
```

## Plotting
```{r}
# Function to create a ggplot for each raster with an individual legend
create_plot <- function(raster_layer, title) {
    # Insert a line break specifically after 'months'
    formatted_title <- gsub("months", "months\n", title, fixed = TRUE)

    p <- gplot(raster_layer) +
        geom_tile(aes(fill = value)) +
        scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "turbo") + # Using Viridis color scale, change as needed
        labs(title = formatted_title, fill = "Value") +
        theme_minimal() +
        theme(
            legend.position = "right", # Adjust legend position as needed
            plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5), # Center the title horizontally
            plot.margin = unit(c(1, 1, 1, 1), "lines"),
            plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white"), # Set plot background color to white
            panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white"), # Set panel background color to white
            panel.grid.major = element_blank(), # Remove major grid lines
            panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), # Remove minor grid lines
            axis.line = element_line(color = "black"), # Set axis line color to black
            axis.text = element_text(color = "black"), # Set axis text color to black
            axis.title = element_text(color = "black") # Set axis title color to black
        ) # Adjust margins around the plots
    return(p)
}
# Create a list of plots
plots_mean <- lapply(raster_data_mean, function(x) create_plot(x, names(x)))

# Use patchwork to combine and arrange all plots
plot_layout_mean <- wrap_plots(plots_mean, ncol = 2) # Adjust the number of columns as needed

# Print the plot layouts
print(plot_layout_mean)
```

## Analysis
```{r}
# Function to multiply each mean raster by the total population raster
multiply_by_population <- function(mean_rasters, population_raster) {
    # Apply the multiplication operation across all rasters in the list
    multiplied_rasters <- lapply(mean_rasters, function(r) {
        # Perform the multiplication
        result_raster <- r * population_raster

        return(result_raster)
    })

    return(multiplied_rasters)
}

# Usage of the function with your mean rasters and total population raster
affected_population_rasters <- multiply_by_population(raster_data_mean, UGA_POPULATION_TOTAL)

# Name the affected population rasters
names(affected_population_rasters) <- paste("pop_affected",
    c(
        "Antenatal_Care_Nonattendance",
        "Health_Insurance_Absence",
        "Postnatal_Care_Nonreceipt",
        "Skilled_Birth_Attendant_Absence",
        "Tetanus_Toxoid_Injection_Absence",
        "Women_Decision_Making_Exclusion",
        "Household_Poverty_Prevalence",
        "Mother_Education_Deprivation"
    ),
    sep = "_"
)

# plot
# Create a list of plots for the affected population rasters
plots_affected_population <- lapply(affected_population_rasters, function(x) create_plot(x, names(x)))

# Use patchwork to combine and arrange all plots
plot_layout_affected_population <- wrap_plots(plots_affected_population, ncol = 2) # Adjust the number of columns as needed

# Print the plot layout
print(plot_layout_affected_population)

```
